Thanks @osterman. CodeRabbit had two findings; both are addressed in the new commit on the branch.

- **`convert.go:160` (introduced by this PR):** Azure passes the deployment name to `SetTokenLimit`, so a deployment called e.g. `o3-backend` that serves `gpt-4o` would have started sending `max_completion_tokens`, which the default Azure API version (`2024-02-15-preview`) does not accept. Azure now uses a new `SetDeploymentTokenLimit`, which keeps the name matching that existed before this PR (`gpt-5*`, `o1-preview`, `o1-mini`, `chatgpt-4o-latest`). The o-series and `gpt-6*` detection applies to the other OpenAI-compatible clients. Tests cover both paths in `openaicompat` and `azureopenai`.
- **`convert.go:151` (Azure deployment alias with no matching name):** this predates the PR: a deployment such as `reasoning-prod` backed by an o-series model gets `max_tokens`, as before. Fixing it needs the underlying model or an explicit setting, which is a config decision, so this PR leaves it as is. A follow-up with an explicit override can be opened if you want one.

`go test` passes for `openaicompat`, `azureopenai` and `openai`.
